sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Cell-surface expression confirmed by surface labelling in HEK293T cells (Supplementary Fig. 1b); full-length ~170 kDa protein detected by anti-HA WB, indicating correct folding and trafficking. Proteolytic-cleavage assays performed on this construct, showing the tagged protein is functional as a substrate for ADAM10/ADAM17, consistent with preserved ectodomain structure.
sites.rationale: The ledger (L1/L2/L3) explicitly states the HA tag is placed after the signal peptide of full-length membrane-anchored CNTNAP2. Python lookup confirms SP ends at residue 27 (T) and the mature extracellular chain begins at residue 28 (A), so insert_after_residue=27 is the exact junction. The construct was confirmed on the cell surface and used in functional cleavage assays, satisfying surface_and_function validation. Distance to TM boundary (residue 1263) is >1200 residues, so steric constraints are trivially met. Full-length human CNTNAP2 (1–1331 aa) expressed as pRK5-HA-CNTNAP2-Flag in HEK293T cells; HA tag inserted immediately after the signal peptide (SP residues 1–27), placing it at the mature extracellular N-terminus (residue 28 onward). Cell-surface expression confirmed by surface biotinylation/immunofluorescence; full-length ~170 kDa band detected by anti-HA, anti-FLAG, and anti-CNTNAP2 antibodies on western blot.

sources.claim: To investigate whether CNTNAP2 undergoes proteolytic cleavage, plasmid pRK5-HA-CNTNAP2-Flag (CNTNAP2 with an HA tag after signal peptide (SP) and a Flag tag at the C-terminus; Supplementary Fig. 1a , upper) was transfected into HEK293T cells, CNTNAP2 was expressed on the cell surface (Supplementary Fig. 1b ).

literature_notes: Three ledger clips (L1, L2, L3) all describe the same dual-tagged construct. L2 is the primary citation for surface confirmation; L1 and L3 corroborate the same junction and the same construct. The C-terminal FLAG tag (after residue 1331) is intracellular (topology: 1284–1331) and is recorded in other_positions. No internal extracellular loop insertions are reported in the ledger for CNTNAP2; no other sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: FLAG tag fused to the C-terminus of full-length CNTNAP2 (residue 1331); the C-terminus lies within the intracellular domain (residues 1284–1331), making this an intracellular label, not a surface tag.
